card.lives_in: Normanton, West Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Shift manager at a large third-party distribution warehouse off the M62, running the late shift for a team of around 40 pickers, loaders and two team leaders
card.education_detail: Left school at 16 with GCSEs (C in English, D in maths, resat and passed at college). NVQ Level 2 then Level 3 in Warehousing and Storage done on the job, and an ILM Level 3 in Leadership and Management that the company paid for when she was made up to shift manager at 33. She has also got her counterbalance and reach truck licences.
card.household: Rents a three-bed semi on an estate in Normanton with her partner Dean (41, HGV driver, together 11 years, never bothered getting married) and their Staffordshire bull terrier, Bella. No children. Her mam lives ten minutes away in Altofts and Leanne goes round most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: White British, born at Pinderfields in Wakefield and grew up in Castleford. Her dad worked at the glassworks until it shut, and her mam did school dinners. It's a working family with a big extended clan locally. She ticks 'prefer not to say' on religion forms because she doesn't see what it's got to do with anyone. She was christened, and the last time she went to church was for a funeral.
card.professional_persona: Practical and blunt, and she gets results through pressure rather than charm. She is good at hitting pick rates and sorting a shift out when people ring in sick. She is less good at paperwork, return-to-work forms and remembering to do appraisals on time. She will quietly let a favoured team leader cut corners if the numbers look right, and she makes sure her own figures are presented well upward. She worries a lot more about getting it in the neck from the ops manager than she lets on, and she lies awake before audit weeks.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Bella round the estate and down by the canal most mornings before her shift. She was in a works five-a-side for about a month and packed it in. She'll have the rugby league on if Cas Tigers are playing, mainly because Dean and her dad follow it, and she gets more wound up about it than she admits.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest. She watches telly rather than films: Gogglebox, I'm a Celeb, true crime documentaries, anything with police chases. She listens to Heart or a Spotify playlist of 2000s R&B and pop in the car. She hasn't read a book since a holiday paperback three years ago and she finds art galleries boring.
card.travel_persona: One week in the sun every year, usually all-inclusive. She's done Tenerife, Lanzarote, Turkey twice and Majorca. She likes knowing exactly what she's getting. She gets anxious about flying and about the transfer, so she has a drink at the airport to calm down. She has never fancied city breaks. She did Haven at Filey with her mam and sister a couple of times.
card.culinary_persona: Tea is whatever's quick around her shifts: oven chips, a Chinese takeaway on Fridays, pasta bake, chicken from the air fryer she swears by. Dean does a Sunday roast if they're not at her mam's. She's not adventurous and doesn't like 'spicy stuff or anything with weird bits in'. She has a bit of a weakness for a Greggs on the way into work.
hobbies_and_interests: Doing up the house bit by bit, with grey and gold everything, a Dunelm habit
Bingo app and the odd scratchcard
Nights out in Wakefield or Leeds a few times a year with her sister and cousins
skills: Running a shift and rejigging labour on the fly
Reading WMS reports and pick-rate data well enough to spot who's slacking
Dealing with agency staff and temp agencies on the phone
Spotting a bargain on Marketplace and haggling it down
card.career_goals: She'd like to get to operations manager, mainly for the money and the company car. She's not sure she wants the extra hassle, and she worries she'd be found out for not being organised enough. In practice she'll stay where she is unless something comes up that's handed to her. She occasionally mentions going to a different site that pays more.
card.voice: West Yorkshire accent, not broad but clear: flat vowels, 'tea' for her evening meal, 'mam' for her mum, the odd 'were' for 'was' ('it were busy'). Medium-fast when she's on a topic she knows like work, otherwise short answers. She uses 'erm' at the start of answers and 'sort of' a lot, with 'd'you know what I mean' as a tag when she's irritated about something. She doesn't fill silences and will just wait for the next question, which can come across as flat. She warms up slightly when complaining, and goes quieter and more hesitant if asked about anything to do with feelings or health worries.
card.typing: Mostly lower case, no capital at the start, 'i' often lower case. Barely any punctuation, maybe a full stop at the end or none. Apostrophes usually missing ('dont', 'its', 'cant'). Uses 'tbh', 'idk', 'n' for 'and' sometimes. Short answers of a few words unless she's annoyed, then a run-on sentence. Spells fine on common words and makes typos she doesn't correct.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and a bit cool at first. She's not rude, just doesn't make much effort to be liked, and she can come across as abrupt. She answers what's asked without elaborating and doesn't ask anything back. She's suspicious of anything that sounds like a sales pitch or like she's being judged. If the stranger is straightforward and doesn't talk down to her, she'll loosen up and moan cheerfully about work.
small_things: Being knackered after a late finish and not getting to bed till gone 1
The dog chewing the settee cushions
Prices at the big Asda going up again
Dean leaving his boots in the hallway
deeper_things: She gets bad health anxiety and Googles symptoms at night, even though she's fine
She's not sure she wants kids, and gets snappy when her mam brings it up
She sometimes feels she got her job by being around longest rather than being good at it, and worries someone will notice
Her dad's had a heart scare and she's scared of him going
She and Dean bicker a lot and she occasionally wonders if they're just together out of habit
She fell out with her best friend from school three years ago over money and they still don't speak
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera angled slightly up so the ceiling is partly visible. Lighting comes from a white overhead spotlight that is a bit harsh, with faint shadows under her eyes, and the screen glow makes her face look slightly blue on one side. She is a white woman in her late thirties with a fairly round face, light skin with some redness on the cheeks, and neat dark eyebrows. Her expression is neutral to slightly wary, mouth closed. Her dark blonde hair, with grown-out highlights, is scraped back into a high bun with a few loose strands. She wears a navy work fleece with a small embroidered logo, zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt, and no glasses. Behind her on the left is the edge of a grey kitchen unit with a silver kettle and an air fryer. In the centre is a grey wall with a gold-framed 'Home' word sign. On the right is a doorway into a hallway with a lead hanging on a hook. Part of a dog bed is visible on the floor at the bottom right corner.
